subject: Renewal capacity request: hot-standby shift + smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Rita Chang <rita@brightpath.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance for upcoming renewal

Hi Sergio,

We're coming up on our annual renewal on Feb 14 and we need help sizing our Dedicated pool. Over the last 90 days our average sustained concurrency for inference has been ~420 concurrent streams with 99th percentile latency spikes tied to peak batch jobs on weekdays. We attached a utilization CSV export (brightpath_utilization_snapshot_202801.csv) showing hourly GPU occupancy and tail latency.

Given those numbers, we want to explore two things:
- Reserving a slab of additional H100 capacity (short term) to reduce 99p latency
- Moving 10% of our current hot-standby hunch (standby nodes) into an active elastic slab with smoother auto-scale thresholds so we don't hit cold-start bursts.

Can your team propose a technical runbook + pricing options? We also need to surface SOC2 evidence for our internal security review during the renewal conversations.

Thanks,
Rita
Rita Chang
Head of Platform Engineering
Brightpath Health
attachments: brightpath_utilization_snapshot_202801.csv
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Rita Chang <rita@brightpath.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance for upcoming renewal

Rita — thanks for the data, this is very helpful. I pulled the CSV and did a first-pass assessment. Short summary:

- 420 sustained concurrent streams maps to approx. 24 x H100 active slots at your observed seq/throughput distribution.
- Spiky weekday batches are driving your 99p latency; adding a 6–8 H100 "smoothing slab" for scheduled batch windows will reduce tail risk by ~35–45%.
- Shifting 10% of your hot-standby to an elastic slab with a narrower cold-start window (we can pre-warm KV caches during known batch windows) looks feasible as a staged runbook.

I've attached a draft SOW + options (BRP-SOW-proposal-2028-01.pdf) and a quick pricing workbook (pricing-options-8xH100.xlsx). Ben, Kimberly — can you review technical and commercial items below and confirm.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment on 2 options: (A) 8xH100 reserved slab + 10% hot-standby->elastic reprofile OR (B) 12xH100 reserved slab and keep current standby.
2) If option A preferred, we schedule a small staged rollout: week 1 pre-warm, week 2 monitor, week 3 finalize commit.
3) Provide SOC2 evidence link for Brightpath review (we'll attach SOC2 report and security questionnaire).

Thanks — I'll hold a 30m call Thursday if that helps to walk through the SOW.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
attachments: BRP-SOW-proposal-2028-01.pdf, pricing-options-8xH100.xlsx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance for upcoming renewal

Sergio — quick technical notes (internal):

On Jan 15, 2028 at 12:45 PM, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai wrote:
> I've attached a draft SOW + options (BRP-SOW-proposal-2028-01.pdf) and a quick pricing workbook (pricing-options-8xH100.xlsx). Ben, Kimberly — can you review technical and commercial items below and confirm.

Readout:
- The 24 x H100 active estimate assumes your current prompt/sequence mix. If Brightpath shifts to longer sequences for batch tasks, we should re-profile to 28–30 x H100.
- For the "elastic slab" reprofile: implement prefix-KV pre-warm hooks that run 30–45 minutes prior to scheduled heavy windows (we can automate via their cron jobs or Redwood scheduler). This reduces cold-start tokens by ~70% in our tests.
- Hot-standby shift: We'll keep a 2-GPU buffer per availability zone for safety during rollout and expose an ops flag to force immediate scale-up for migrations.
- Observability: add a per-slot 99th latency alert and an auto-fallback policy to the cheaper model variant so user-facing traffic stays healthy if slab fills.

I'll add these as a technical appendix to the SOW. For SOC2 evidence, I'll attach the report and a short mapping doc showing where Brightpath's questions map to our controls.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product — Enterprise Features, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Rita Chang <rita@brightpath.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance for upcoming renewal

Rita — thanks for the context and to Sergio/Kim for the technical notes. Commercial options (all $ amounts are monthly list and can be negotiated in the renewal contract):

Option A (Preferred - staged):
- 8 x H100 reserved slab: $98,400/mo
- Elastic reprofile + pre-warm automation (operational fee): $6,000/mo
- Commitment term: 12 months (discount applied in final contract)

Option B (Higher reserve):
- 12 x H100 reserved slab: $146,800/mo
- Keep existing standby configuration: no ops fee

Operational notes:
- We can structure a 3-month ramp with a 30% usage-based credit window to allow Brightpath to test the pre-warm flows before final commitment.
- If you need immediate reduction in 99p latency for a short campaign, there's a short-term burst credit package (30k tokens equivalent) we can add for the first 60 days.

Please let us know which option you prefer. If you sign for Option A this week we can schedule the pre-warm and observability dashboards to be live by Feb 1 to validate before your renewal date.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing-options-8xH100.xlsx

Ben / Sergio / Kim — appreciate the rapid turn. After a quick internal review Marcus and I are inclined to move forward with Option A (8xH100 + elastic reprofile) with the 3-month ramp credit you proposed. Two asks before we sign:

1) Please share the SOC2 report and the control-mapping doc for our security team (we need those attached to the PO).
2) Can you include a clause in the SOW that guarantees the pre-warm window will be automated and that Redwood will monitor a 99p latency improvement metric during the 3-month ramp? We need a clear rollback/fallback in writing.

If you can send an updated SOW with those two items and a final monthly rate (net of the ramp credit) we can get the PO out by Jan 26.

Thanks,
Rita
Rita Chang
Head of Platform Engineering
Brightpath Health
